claim: On May 6, 2025 EBS added Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization: you set an initialization rate when you create a volume so that it is fully initialized in a predictable amount of time.
question: When did EBS add Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization, and what does it give you?

values.display: fully initialized in a predictable amount of time

evidence.quote: | [Amazon EBS Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/initalize-volume.html) | You can now specify a volume initialization rate when you create Amazon EBS volumes to make sure that they are fully initialized in a predictable amount of time. | May 6, 2025 |

claim: If you specify a volume initialization rate and the snapshot is enabled for fast snapshot restore, EBS uses the specified rate instead of fast snapshot restore; to use fast snapshot restore, leave the rate out.
question: What happens if you set a volume initialization rate on a snapshot that has fast snapshot restore enabled?

values.display: uses the specified rate instead of fast snapshot restore

qualifiers.scope: per volume created from a snapshot

evidence.quote: If you specify a volume initialization rate and use a snapshot that is enabled for fast snapshot restore, Amazon EBS uses the specified rate instead of fast snapshot restore. To use fast snapshot restore instead, do not specify a volume initialization rate.

claim: With a volume initialization rate you pay a per-GiB rate for the selected initialization tier, based on the full snapshot data size, not the size of the volume.
question: What is the charge for Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization based on?

values.display: full snapshot data size, not the size of the volume

qualifiers.scope: per volume created with an initialization rate

evidence.quote: When you create a volume with a volume initialization rate, you are charged a per-GiB rate based on the selected initialization tier. The rate varies by Region.
You are charged based on the full snapshot data size, not the size of the volume.

claim: On November 26, 2024 EBS added time-based snapshot copies: you request a completion duration so that a snapshot copy finishes within a specific timeframe.
question: When did EBS add time-based snapshot copies?

evidence.quote: | [Time-based snapshot copies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/time-based-copies.html) | You can now request a completion duration for snapshot copy operations to make sure that snapshot copies are completed within a specific timeframe. | November 26, 2024 |

claim: On February 25, 2025 the completion duration was extended to EBS-backed AMI copy operations.
question: When did time-based copies become available for EBS-backed AMIs?

evidence.quote: | [Time-based AMI copies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/time-based-copies.html) | You can now request a completion duration for EBS-backed AMI copy operations to make sure that AMI copies are completed within a specific timeframe. | February 25, 2025 |

claim: For a time-based snapshot or EBS-backed AMI copy you specify a completion duration between 15 minutes and 48 hours, in 15 minute increments.
question: What completion durations can you request for a time-based snapshot copy?

values.spoken: between fifteen minutes and forty-eight hours

evidence.quote: With time-based snapshot and EBS-backed AMI copy operations, you specify a completion duration, between 15 minutes and 48 hours, in which the copy is to be completed. The completion duration must be specified in 15 minute increments.

claim: Time-based copies make snapshot and AMI copies, within and across Regions, finish in a specified timeframe, which helps meet disaster recovery RPO and RTO requirements.
question: Why would you use a time-based snapshot copy instead of a standard copy?

evidence.quote: Time-based copies can help you meet compliance or business requirements for data replication by ensuring that your EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs are copied, within and across AWS Regions, in a specified timeframe. Time-based copies can also help backup administrators meet stringent disaster recovery requirements (Recovery Point Objectives and Recovery Time Objectives), and it improves development agility by ensuring predictable copying times for snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs.

claim: Time-based copy operations have an additional charge per GiB of snapshot data copied, at a rate that depends on the requested completion duration.
question: How are time-based snapshot copies charged?

values.display: per GiB of snapshot data copied
based on the requested completion duration

evidence.quote: Additional charges apply for time-based snapshot and EBS-backed AMI copy operations. Time-based copy operations are charged at a rate that is based on the requested completion duration, per GiB of snapshot data copied.

claim: When you copy a snapshot to a new Region, the first copy is a full (non-incremental) copy with additional storage costs; later copies of the same snapshot are incremental.
question: Is the first copy of a snapshot to another Region incremental?

values.display: Subsequent copies of the same snapshot are incremental

qualifiers.scope: per snapshot copied to a new Region
qualifiers.condition: cross-Region data transfer charges also apply

evidence.quote: Similar to standard snapshot copy operations, if you copy a snapshot to a new Region, a full (non-incremental) copy is created, which results in additional storage costs. Subsequent copies of the same snapshot are incremental.

claim: On November 9, 2023 EBS added block public access for snapshots, which prevents the public sharing of your snapshots.
question: When did EBS add block public access for snapshots?

evidence.quote: | [Block public access for snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/block-public-access-snapshots.html) | You can now use block public access for snapshots to prevent the public sharing of your snapshots. | November 9, 2023 |

claim: On December 1, 2024 declarative policies in AWS Organizations became able to apply the block public access setting for snapshots across many Regions and accounts at once.
question: When could block public access for EBS snapshots be set with an AWS Organizations declarative policy?

values.display: across multiple Regions and accounts simultaneously

evidence.quote: | [Declarative policies for block public access for EBS snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/block-public-access-snapshots.html) | You can now use declarative policies to apply account-level settings for block public access for snapshots across multiple Regions and accounts simultaneously. For more information, see [Declarative policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_declarative.html) in the *AWS Organizations User Guide*. | December 1, 2024 |

claim: After you enable block public access for snapshots in a Region, any attempt to publicly share snapshots in that Region is automatically blocked.
question: What does block public access for EBS snapshots do?

values.display: any attempt to publicly share snapshots

evidence.quote: After you enable block public access for snapshots in a Region, any attempt to publicly share snapshots in that Region is automatically blocked.

claim: Block public access for snapshots is a Regional setting: you must enable it in each Region where you want to prevent public sharing of snapshots.
question: Does enabling block public access for snapshots in one Region protect snapshots in other Regions?

values.display: enable block public access for snapshots in each Region

qualifiers.condition: a declarative policy can apply it across Regions and accounts

evidence.quote: Block public access for snapshots is a Regional setting. It applies to all snapshots in the Region in which it is enabled. You need to enable block public access for snapshots in each Region in which you want to prevent the public sharing of your snapshots.

claim: Block public access for snapshots does not prevent public sharing of EBS-backed AMIs; to stop that, you enable block public access for AMIs.
question: Does block public access for snapshots also stop public sharing of EBS-backed AMIs?

values.display: does not prevent the public sharing of EBS-backed AMIs

evidence.quote: Block public access for snapshots does not prevent the public sharing of EBS-backed AMIs. If you enable block public access for snapshots, users can still publicly share EBS-backed AMIs.

claim: Block public access for snapshots can be enabled at no additional cost.
question: What does block public access for EBS snapshots cost?

evidence.quote: Block public access for snapshots can be enabled at no additional cost.

claim: On November 15, 2023 EBS added snapshot lock, which protects snapshots against accidental or malicious deletion and can store them in WORM format for a specific duration.
question: When did EBS add snapshot lock?

evidence.quote: | [Amazon EBS snapshot lock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshot-lock.html) | You can lock your Amazon EBS snapshots to protect them against accidental or malicious deletions, or to or store them in WORM format for a specific duration. | November 15, 2023 |

claim: While a snapshot is locked, no user can delete it, whatever their IAM permissions; you can still use the locked snapshot like any other snapshot.
question: Can an administrator with full IAM permissions delete a locked EBS snapshot?

values.display: it can't be deleted by any user

qualifiers.condition: while the lock is in effect

evidence.quote: While a snapshot is locked, it can't be deleted by any user, regardless of their IAM permissions. You can continue to use a locked snapshot in the same way that you would use any other snapshot.

claim: You lock a snapshot in compliance mode or governance mode, for a specific duration or until a specific date.
question: Which modes does EBS snapshot lock have?

values.display: for a specific duration or until a specific date

evidence.quote: You can lock snapshots in one of two modes: *compliance mode* or *governance mode*, and they can be locked for a specific duration or until a specific date.

claim: Locking and unlocking snapshots has no additional cost; you pay the standard snapshot storage costs for locked snapshots.
question: What does EBS snapshot lock cost?

values.display: standard Amazon EBS snapshot storage costs

evidence.quote: You can lock and unlock snapshots at no additional cost. You pay the standard Amazon EBS snapshot storage costs for locked snapshots.

claim: On November 16, 2023 Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager added default policies for EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs that back up all volumes and instances in a Region.
question: When did Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager add default policies?

values.display: backup all volumes and instances in a Region

evidence.quote: | [Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager default policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/policy-differences.html) | You can now create Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager default policies for EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs to backup all volumes and instances in a Region. | November 16, 2023 |

claim: On November 7, 2023 Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager snapshot policies gained pre and post scripts to automate application-consistent snapshots.
question: When could Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager automate application-consistent snapshots with scripts?

evidence.quote: | [Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager pre and post scripts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/automate-app-consistent-backups.html) | You can now use pre and post scripts in your Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager snapshot policies to automate the lifecycle of application-consistent snapshots. | November 7, 2023 |

claim: On September 18, 2023 Multi-Attach enabled io2 volumes gained support for NVMe reservations, a set of industry-standard storage fencing protocols.
question: When did Multi-Attach io2 volumes gain NVMe reservations?

evidence.quote: | [NVMe reservations](#doc-history) | Multi-Attach enabled `io2` volumes support NVMe reservations, which is a set of industry-standard storage fencing protocols. | September 18, 2023 |

claim: A Multi-Attach enabled io1 or io2 volume can be attached to up to 16 Nitro-based instances in the same Availability Zone; otherwise an EBS volume attaches to a single instance.
question: To how many instances can one Multi-Attach EBS volume be attached?

qualifiers.scope: per Multi-Attach enabled io1 or io2 volume
qualifiers.condition: instances in the same Availability Zone

evidence.quote: You can attach `io1` and `io2` EBS volumes to up to 16 Nitro-based instances.
Amazon EBS Multi-Attach enables you to attach a single Provisioned IOPS SSD (`io1` or `io2`) volume to multiple instances that are in the same Availability Zone.

note: FRESHNESS d114 checked: no history row since 2020 changes the 16-instance, same-AZ, io1/io2-only rule; the only later row (2023-09-18) adds NVMe reservations.

claim: Multi-Attach has no additional charge; you pay the standard charges of the io1 or io2 volume.
question: Does EBS Multi-Attach cost extra?

values.display: no additional charges for using Amazon EBS Multi-Attach

evidence.quote: There are no additional charges for using Amazon EBS Multi-Attach. You are billed the standard charges that apply to Provisioned IOPS SSD (`io1` and `io2`) volumes.
